claim: Swi2/Snf2 ATPases are members of the NTP-dependent helicase/translocase superfamily 2 (SF2).

evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

evidence: This is based on structural modeling and comparison.

claim: Superimposing SsoRad54:DNA with CtMot1∆C via lobe 1 visualizes how the CtMot1 ATPase could initially contact duplex DNA.
source: Likewise, superimposing SsoRad54:DNA with CtMot1∆C via lobe 1 visualizes how the CtMot1 ATPase could initially contact duplex DNA since in all Snf2/Swi2 protein:substrate structures contacts between nucleic acid and the RecA1 subdomain are preserved.
evidence: This is based on structural modeling and comparison.

claim: In all Snf2/Swi2 protein:substrate structures, contacts between nucleic acid and the RecA1 subdomain are preserved.

evidence: This is established knowledge about Snf2/Swi2 protein structures.

claim: The localization and orientation of the Swi2/Snf2 domain in the model is in full agreement with prior EM and CX-MS analyses.
source: In the resulting model, localization and orientation of the Swi2/Snf2 domain is in full agreement with prior EM and CX-MS analyses (Butryn et al., 2015) and with biochemical studies showing that Mot1 covers two helical turns upstream from the TATA box (Darst et al., 2001; Sprouse et al., 2006; Moyle-Heyrman et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by comparison with prior studies cited.

claim: The localization and orientation of the Swi2/Snf2 domain in the model is in agreement with biochemical studies showing that Mot1 covers two helical turns upstream from the TATA box.
source: In the resulting model, localization and orientation of the Swi2/Snf2 domain is in full agreement with prior EM and CX-MS analyses (Butryn et al., 2015) and with biochemical studies showing that Mot1 covers two helical turns upstream from the TATA box (Darst et al., 2001; Sprouse et al., 2006; Moyle-Heyrman et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by comparison with prior studies cited.

claim: The superimposed DNA segment bound by the ATPase is an almost direct continuation of the promoter DNA fragment from the EcMot1NTD:TBP:NC2:DNA crystal structure.
source: Notably, the superimposed DNA segment bound by the ATPase is an almost direct continuation of the promoter DNA fragment from the EcMot1NTD:TBP:NC2:DNA crystal structure.
evidence: This is based on structural modeling.

claim: The structure of CtMot1 and the specific orientation of lobe 1 suggests that the Swi2/Snf2 motor translocates 'towards' the TATA box and TBP along the nucleic acid scaffold.
source: Assuming the generally proposed directionality of ATP dependent translocation of Swi2/Snf2 motor domains on dsDNA (Zofall et al., 2006; Saha et al., 2002; Whitehouse et al., 2003), the structure of CtMot1 and the specific orientation of lobe 1 now suggests that the Swi2/Snf2 motor translocates 'towards' the TATA box and TBP along the nucleic acid scaffold.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural data and knowledge of Swi2/Snf2 translocation directionality.

claim: Processive ATP-dependent translocase activity has not been observed in biochemical studies of Mot1.
source: Since processive ATP-dependent translocase activity has not been observed in biochemical studies, Mot1 could exploit short-range tracking toward TBP.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of biochemical knowledge.

claim: Mot1 could exploit short-range tracking toward TBP.
source: Since processive ATP-dependent translocase activity has not been observed in biochemical studies, Mot1 could exploit short-range tracking toward TBP.
evidence: This is speculation based on the structural model and biochemical knowledge.

claim: Very few translocation steps could lead to the displacement of TBP by steric collision given the immediate vicinity of the Swi2/Snf2 domain to TBP.
source: Given the immediate vicinity of the Swi2/Snf2 domain to TBP, very few translocation steps could lead to the displacement of TBP by steric collision (Darst et al., 2001; Auble and Steggerda, 1999; Butryn et al., 2015).
evidence: This is speculation based on the structural model and supported by citations.

claim: Mot1 could simply displace TBP from DNA by overwinding or introducing other small distortions into upstream DNA.
source: In addition, Mot1 could simply displace TBP from DNA by overwinding or introducing other small distortions into upstream DNA (Moyle-Heyrman et al., 2012; Butryn et al., 2015).
evidence: This is speculation based on the structural model and supported by citations.

claim: Similar effects have been observed for other transcription factors, for which not only binding but also dissociation rates depend on the structure of their recognition sites affected by the presence of other factors bound nearby.
source: Similar effects have been observed for other transcription factors, for which not only binding but also dissociation rates depend on the structure of their recognition sites affected by the presence of other factors bound nearby (Luo et al., 2014; Kim et al., 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The allosteric effect can be accounted for by local changes to the major and minor groove width.
source: This allosteric effect can be accounted for by local changes to the major and minor groove width (Kim et al., 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Changes two helical turns upstream from the TBP binding site could have an immediate allosteric effect on severely bent and widened TATA box.
source: Such a scenario is plausible since changes two helical turns upstream from the TBP binding site could have an immediate allosteric effect on severely bent and widened TATA box (Tora and Timmers, 2010).
evidence: This is speculation based on structural considerations and supported by a citation.

claim: Mot1's ATPase orientation suggests that it 'pulls' DNA from TBP and overwinds DNA at the substrate.
source: Interestingly, while Mot1's ATPase orientation suggests that it 'pulls' DNA from TBP and overwinds DNA at the substrate, the reverse architecture is seen for the multisubunit INO80 remodeler: here the motor appears to pump DNA into the nucleosome and to underwind DNA at the substrate (Eustermann et al., 2018).
evidence: This is inferred from the structural model.

claim: The reverse architecture is seen for the multisubunit INO80 remodeler: the motor appears to pump DNA into the nucleosome and to underwind DNA at the substrate.
